idea.en: Find the apex and open all four chambers.

note.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle

steps.en: What you see: All four chambers open with the septa near vertical and the left ventricle capped by a tapering apex on the right of the image. The mitral and tricuspid valves sit at slightly different heights, the tricuspid nearer the apex.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values: Left ventricular ejection fraction 52 percent or above in men and 54 percent or above in women is normal, below 30 percent is severely reduced.
Left atrial volume index below 34 ml per sq m is normal.
Average E over e prime below 14 suggests normal filling pressure.

Pitfalls: Foreshortening is the commonest error in this view and it flatters function, so length comes before any measurement. The moderator band in the right ventricle is normal muscle, not thrombus.
Indian context: Rheumatic mitral stenosis enlarges the left atrium early, so an adult Indian patient with breathlessness and a large left atrium in this view needs a full mitral workup.

analogy.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle

spot.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of left ventricle

Common mistakes and how to correct them: Foreshortened apex that understates length and overstates function. Correct it by moving the probe to the true point of maximal impulse until the ventricle is at its longest.
Aorta in view meaning the plane has rotated too anterior. Correct it by rotating back toward the posterior until the aorta disappears.
Septum too horizontal from a lateral apex position. Correct it by sliding medially until the septum stands near vertical.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at apex, fifth intercostal space at the midclavicular line.
Point the probe marker toward the left, about three o clock.
Feel the apex beat and put the probe there first, then slide until the septum stands vertical and the apex is at its longest. If the aorta appears, you have rotated too far anterior.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Grade left ventricular function by eye before measuring.

q.en: Where does the probe sit for the four chamber?

why.en: The four chamber starts at the apex beat in the fifth space at the midclavicular line.

q.en: Left atrial volume index is 42 ml per sq m. What does this mean?

why.en: Above 34 ml per sq m the atrium is dilated by definition.

q.en: The aorta appears in the four chamber. What went wrong?

why.en: The aorta enters when the plane rotates anterior toward the five chamber.
